title: TUI history pane scrolls through the item's whole history
lead: The history pane (s278) shows only the item's newest 20 entries and cannot scroll; let it take focus and scroll like the relay board.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** scrolling the dependencies pane; a project-wide history view; caching the log between redraws.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: s278's history pane calls `history_lines(state, target, HISTORY_LIMIT)` with `HISTORY_LIMIT = 20` (`src/slicer/tui.py:433`), and `tab` stays in the queue while it is shown (`View.handle`, the `pane` action), so an item with a long relay history loses its older starts, handoffs and rejects, and a short terminal clips even those 20. The relay board already scrolls with `board_at` and j/k (`src/slicer/tui.py:930`). Raised as a later note by the s278 gate, 2026-10-17.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/tui.py`: a `history_at` offset on `View`; in the history pane `tab` moves focus to the pane, j/k and arrows move `history_at`, clamped as `board_at` is in `draw()`; selecting another item or cycling `i` resets it. `history_lines` stops truncating to 20 (or the limit rises), and `draw()` slices from `history_at`.
- `docs/tui.md` (Dependencies and history), `CHANGELOG.md`, `tests/test_tui.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Handle_HistoryPaneFocused_DownScrollsHistory`
- `test_Handle_SelectOtherItem_ResetsHistoryScroll`
- `test_Draw_HistoryScrolled_ShowsOlderEntries` (a curses stub as the existing draw tests use)
- `e` in the focused history pane still says it is read-only.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the offset, the focus rule and the scroll keys; drop the 20-entry cap.
3. Update the docs and CHANGELOG. Mutation-check each new test.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full discover. `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
